subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw make a positive Docker sandbox `pidsLimit` the default for existing unset configs, and what unlimited or Docker-default opt-out contract must ship with it?
rationale: The source-reproducible hardening is useful, but changing an effective sandbox default can break existing deployments and crosses a security-versus-compatibility boundary that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof show fresh behavior, upgrade behavior, and explicit override semantics.

options.title: Keep default unset
options.body: Preserve current upgrade behavior and document operator-configured `pidsLimit` instead of changing existing unset deployments.

options.title: Make strict cap opt-in
options.body: Use an explicit strict profile or setting if maintainers want the mitigation without changing current unset configs.

recommendation.title: Approve default with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the default-on PID cap only after schema/type/docs/tests and real Docker proof show fresh behavior, upgrade behavior, and explicit override semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the sandbox runtime/security surfaces to this team, and the decision is a sandbox security boundary default.
